wa_bacon_peak_diobsud.name: Wilderness-boundary saddle
wa_bacon_peak_diobsud.note: Trail forks here — right drops 0.5mi to Lower Anderson Lake, left climbs into the Noisy-Diobsud Wilderness toward Watson Lakes.

wa_bacon_peak_diobsud.name: Watson Lakes
wa_bacon_peak_diobsud.note: Last reliable water and the only legal campsites before the cross-country push into Diobsud basin; designated sites only, campfires prohibited.

wa_bacon_peak_diobsud.name: Diobsud basin
wa_bacon_peak_diobsud.note: Off-trail descent from the Watson/Diobsud divide into the Diobsud Creek drainage; trip reports say to drop straight to the valley floor rather than contouring from the lakes, which is slower.

wa_bacon_peak_diobsud.name: Access gully to Diobsud Creek Glacier
wa_bacon_peak_diobsud.note: Loose rock and slick dirt in the chute leading to the glacier's toe once snow has melted out — trip reports describe clawing up steep, loose dirt gullies here.

wa_bacon_peak_diobsud.name: Diobsud Creek Glacier crossing
wa_bacon_peak_diobsud.note: Rope up here — crevasses open on the icecap by mid-to-late season; probe and stay roped through to the saddle below the summit block.

wa_bacon_peak_diobsud.name: Watson Lakes Trailhead
wa_bacon_peak_diobsud.note: Existing DB trailhead (Anderson and Watson Lakes Trailhead, 48.6749/-121.6153) is a real, well-documented trailhead but serves the separate NE-side Green Lake Glacier / Watson Lakes approach, not the Diobsud Creek Glacier side this route is named for. Recommend correcting to this SE-side Bacon Creek Road trailhead, which matches the route's own recorded track almost exactly.

wa_bryant_peak_southeast_slopes.name: Source Lake Trail junction
wa_bryant_peak_southeast_slopes.note: Signed junction on Snow Lake Trail #1013; leave the main trail here and head toward Source Lake basin (on-file mileage).

wa_bryant_peak_southeast_slopes.name: Source Lake basin stream crossing
wa_bryant_peak_southeast_slopes.note: Climbers' path fords the outlet stream draining Source Lake basin around 4,100 ft; last reliable water before the ascent gully, cairns mark the crossing.

wa_bryant_peak_southeast_slopes.name: Gully 'secret passage' below the cliffs
wa_bryant_peak_southeast_slopes.note: Trip-report landmark: an easy-to-miss rock passage at ~4,780 ft where the route leaves the open streambed gully and climbs NE along cliff bands into the upper basin.

wa_bryant_peak_southeast_slopes.name: Thumbtack (rock tower), upper basin
wa_bryant_peak_southeast_slopes.note: Prominent free-standing rock tower marking the talus basin between Bryant and Chair Peak; from here the route corkscrews southwest toward the Bryant-Chair gully.

wa_bryant_peak_southeast_slopes.name: Bryant-Chair Peak gully / talus shoulder
wa_bryant_peak_southeast_slopes.note: Steep, loose gully between the two peaks gains a talus shoulder on Bryant's ridge; helmets recommended, rockfall risk from parties above.

wa_bryant_peak_southeast_slopes.name: Summit block traverse
wa_bryant_peak_southeast_slopes.note: Route stays left (south) of the talus field and traverses the south side of the west shoulder before the final scramble; exposed with loose rock, though holds are generally good.

wa_bryant_peak_southeast_slopes.name: Alpental / Snow Lake Trailhead (I-90 Exit 52)
wa_bryant_peak_southeast_slopes.note: Existing DB trailhead 'Snow Lake / Alpental Trailhead' (47.44542, -121.42353) appears to be wrong for this route — it's a different drainage ~3km away with no sourced connection to Bryant Peak. Denny Creek TH matches the recorded GPS track's start point (47.4152566, -121.4433387) almost exactly (~<100m), and multiple sources describe the Denny Creek Trail -> Hemlock Pass -> ridge -> SE talus field approach used specifically for this Southeast Slopes route.

wa_glacier_peak_kennedy_glacier.name: White Chuck River Trail (FST 643) / Kennedy Ridge Trail (FST 639) junction
wa_glacier_peak_kennedy_glacier.note: Leave the river trail here and start climbing Kennedy Ridge Trail toward the PCT.

wa_glacier_peak_kennedy_glacier.name: Kennedy Ridge Trail / PCT junction
wa_glacier_peak_kennedy_glacier.note: Kennedy Ridge Trail meets the PCT about a quarter mile north of Kennedy Creek; turn to follow the PCT toward Glacier Creek.

wa_glacier_peak_kennedy_glacier.name: Glacier Creek PCT crossing camp
wa_glacier_peak_kennedy_glacier.note: Good established campsites with reliable creek water about 2 miles along the PCT from the Kennedy Ridge junction.

wa_glacier_peak_kennedy_glacier.name: Ridge saddle above camp
wa_glacier_peak_kennedy_glacier.note: Climb SSE up the basin from the Glacier Creek camp to this flat saddle where the route gains the open slopes below Kennedy Glacier.

wa_glacier_peak_kennedy_glacier.name: Vista-Kennedy saddle
wa_glacier_peak_kennedy_glacier.note: Saddle between Vista Ridge and the Kennedy Glacier icefall; rope up for glacier travel from here.

wa_glacier_peak_kennedy_glacier.name: Kennedy Glacier crevasse band
wa_glacier_peak_kennedy_glacier.note: Deep, dramatic crevasses form on this small, steep glacier; parties often hug the left wall under Kennedy Peak to dodge crevasses at the cost of added rockfall exposure.

wa_glacier_peak_kennedy_glacier.name: White Chuck River Trailhead
wa_glacier_peak_kennedy_glacier.note: Road-end trailhead on Suiattle River Rd (FR 26), ~23.5 mi from Darrington; North Fork Sauk TH (48.05832,-121.28793) is a valid alternate approach for this route.

wa_mount_rainier_ptarmigan_ridge.name: Liberty Cap (commonly the route's summit point)

wa_prusik_peak_west_ridge.name: Stuart Lake Trailhead (Trail #1599)
wa_prusik_peak_west_ridge.note: Also reachable via the Stuart Lake/Colchuck Lake Trailhead (~47.528,-120.820) over Aasgard Pass — a genuinely different, commonly-used alternate approach — but this route's own recorded GPS track starts at Snow Lakes TH, not Stuart Lake TH.

wa_storm_king_southwest_scramble.name: Skagit Queen Camp
wa_storm_king_southwest_scramble.note: Established camp near old Skagit Queen mine workings where the trail steepens into switchbacks; reliable creek water, common first- or second-night stop.

wa_storm_king_southwest_scramble.name: Park Creek Pass
wa_storm_king_southwest_scramble.note: Trail high point in the notch between Mt. Logan and Mt. Buckner; camping is prohibited at the pass itself to protect fragile meadows, so continue on or camp just below it.

wa_storm_king_southwest_scramble.name: Rib camp below Storm King/Goode basin
wa_storm_king_southwest_scramble.note: Flat, grassy camp on a small NE/SW-trending rib south of Storm King with a nearby water source; leave the maintained trail here and go cross-country toward the peak.

wa_storm_king_southwest_scramble.name: Talus cirque beneath the towers
wa_storm_king_southwest_scramble.note: About a mile of loose talus/scree past the rib camp brings you into the cirque directly under Storm King's west and east towers; take the path of least resistance up the scree.

wa_storm_king_southwest_scramble.name: North-side exposed ledge traverse
wa_storm_king_southwest_scramble.note: Class 3-4 ledge system traversing the backside of the summit towers, including a slight overhang requiring a squeeze-under move; most parties fix a line here.

wa_storm_king_southwest_scramble.name: Summit crux crack
wa_storm_king_southwest_scramble.note: 15-foot crack (Class 4 to low 5th) leads to the fixed rappel anchor used for the descent; rope up or belay through this section.

wa_storm_king_southwest_scramble.name: Colonial Creek Campground Trailhead
wa_storm_king_southwest_scramble.note: Drive-to trailhead on SR-20 at Rainy Pass (milepost ~158); hike south on the Bridge Creek Trail/PCT ~9.5 mi (with ~2000 ft loss) to North Fork Group Camp, then leave trail cross-country toward the basin south of Storm King. Some parties instead approach from the south via the Lady of the Lake ferry to Stehekin + shuttle to High Bridge Camp, joining the same Bridge Creek/North Fork trail system. The current DB trailhead (Thunder Creek Trailhead / Colonial Creek Campground, ~48.6855,-121.0925) is a different, unconnected drainage well north of here and is very likely wrong.

wa_unnamed_5.name: SR-20 Hairpin / Pond Pullout (east of Washington Pass)
wa_unnamed_5.note: Park at the hairpin turn pullout on Hwy 20 near Washington Pass; ~7 min uphill approach trail to the base of Spire Gully.

wa_the_rake_traverse_route.name: Goodell Creek Branch Crossings
wa_the_rake_traverse_route.note: Climbers' path fords two branches of Goodell Creek on the old roadbed; can run high and fast during snowmelt.

wa_the_rake_traverse_route.name: Terror Creek Basin Cairn Turnoff
wa_the_rake_traverse_route.note: A stone cairn marks where the boot path leaves the old roadbed and begins climbing steeply into the Terror Creek drainage.

wa_the_rake_traverse_route.name: Terror Creek Basin Camp
wa_the_rake_traverse_route.note: Established campsite about 400 ft below a 6,200-ft saddle, with views of The Barrier, Degenhardt, Pyramid and the McMillan Spires.

wa_the_rake_traverse_route.name: The Barrier
wa_the_rake_traverse_route.note: Steep, loose grassy ledge near 6,100 ft leading to serious class-3 scrambling on rotten rock to gain the crest around 6,400 ft.

wa_the_rake_traverse_route.name: Crescent Creek Basin High Camp
wa_the_rake_traverse_route.note: High camp on the south side of Mount Terror, reached via an easy snow-ramp descent off the Barrier notch; also where enchainment parties arrive via the Otto-Himmel col.

wa_the_rake_traverse_route.name: Rubble Gully to the Terror-Rake Col
wa_the_rake_traverse_route.note: Loose, rubble-choked gully leads to the notch between Mount Terror and The Rake; stay right on slightly harder class-3 rock to dodge the worst debris.

wa_the_rake_traverse_route.name: Goodell Creek / Upper Goodell Group Camp trailhead (SR-20, Newhalem)
wa_the_rake_traverse_route.note: Standard cross-country-zone access for Southern Pickets objectives (Terror Basin/Crescent Creek Basin); existing DB value confirmed correct — close to recorded track start (~1.1km away, consistent with parking-to-cross-country-route offset).
